$comment: The inventory of tests allowed to skip, and why.
A skipped test is a test that is not running. '94 passed, 1 skipped' and
'88 passed, 7 skipped' are nearly indistinguishable in a summary line that
somebody is scanning at speed, so a suite can quietly stop checking things
while every run stays green. That has already happened once here: a stale
.next made six prerender assertions vanish and the run still reported
So CI asserts the skip count per package against this file, not only the
pass count. A skip appearing OR disappearing fails until someone updates
the inventory — which is the point: the update is where the thinking
happens. Disappearing matters as much as appearing, because a skip that
stops skipping usually means the condition guarding it changed.
scripts/check-skips.mjs is the checker. See Prompt 0 in docs/code-prompts.md.

allowed.name: build output is absent — run `pnpm --filter @ledger/clinician build` to check prerendering
allowed.why: The inverse guard in test/build.test.ts. Exactly one of the two blocks in that file runs: with a build present the six prerender assertions run and this one skips; with no build it reports the absence and the six skip. In CI the app is always built first, so this is the one that skips — and build.test.ts throws rather than skips if CI has no build, so the six can never be the skipped half here.
